newsitem.title: GERMANY: German airports demand strict ground handling rule.
newsitem.headline: German airports demand strict ground handling rule.

text.p: Germany should impose strict conditions on de-regulation of airport ground handling services, the country's airports association (ADV) said.
Bonn should take ADV's special situation into account when bringing the new EU airport ground handling rules into German law.
The EU agreed on October 15 to a staged liberalisation of services such as passenger check-ins, airport ramp services, cargo and baggage handling with complete de-regulation by 2003.

ADV, which represents 16 international airports in Germany, said in a statement: "Airports now expect their special situation to carry appropriate weight in the conversion of the EU guideline into German law."
The association said there has always been competition on the "land" side of German airports in areas such as passenger check-ins.
But competition on the "air" side has been resisted out of fears of reduced capacity and financial losses which would affect infrastructure investment.
ADV said Bonn should restrict the number of competitors able to operate in the ramp area to ensure smooth operations and efficient use of infrastructure.
Permission to operate should depend on a reliability check covering safety and training standards, it said.
Fees charged to ground handling companies for airport infrastructure use should be sufficient to ensure airports remain self-financing, ADV said.
Bonn should also ensure qualified jobs will be maintained to prevent any "social dumping".
German airports will now rise to the challenges of an open market and maintain their high ground handling standards, ADV added.
